# package reference

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/reference"
```

Package reference parses, validates and formats IEC 61850 object references.

Two forms are distinguished:

  - [Ref](#type-ref), an instance reference as used on a device: "LD0/MMXU1.Hz.mag.f\[MX]". Its format and validation rules are those of the Ref type of github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850, so values convert between the packages field by field.
  - [ClassRef](#type-classref), a class reference into the normative model: "MMXU.Hz.mag.f\[MX]".

This package checks syntax only. Three levels of validity apply to a reference, and each needs a different source:

 1. Syntax: [Parse](#func-parse), [ParseClass](#func-parseclass) and the Validate methods.
 2. Model validity: the logical node class, data objects and data attributes exist in a namespace profile with the requested functional constraint. The resolver package checks this.
 3. Presence on a device: an optional data object may or may not be implemented. Only SCL or device discovery can tell; the model catalog cannot.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// MaxLNPrefixInstance bounds the LN-Prefix plus LN-Instance-ID
	// (m+n ≤ 12).
	MaxLNPrefixInstance = 12
	// MaxDataObjectName bounds a DataObjectName (≤ 12 characters).
	MaxDataObjectName = 12
	// MaxFCDALength bounds an FCD or FCDA without FC and LD name,
	// including the "." separators (≤ 61 characters).
	MaxFCDALength = 61
)
```

Name limits of IEC 61850-7-2:2010 §22.2, checked by [Ref.ValidateNames](#func-ref-validatenames).

```go
const (
	MaxLDLength   = 64
	MaxPathLength = 64
)
```

MaxLDLength is the maximum length of a logical device name, and MaxPathLength the maximum length of the path below it (LN.DO.DA), IEC 61850-7-2:2010 Table 4: at most 64 characters each, joined by a single "/".

```go
const MaxMMSIdentifier = 64
```

MaxMMSIdentifier is the MMS maxIdentifier size that bounds MMS domain and object names, IEC 61850-8-1:2011 §8.1.3.2.2 (see F.3.2).

```go
const MaxStrictLength = 129
```

MaxStrictLength is the maximum length of an ObjectReference enforced by [ParseStrict](#func-parsestrict): IEC 61850-7-2:2010 Table 4 types ObjectReference as VISIBLE STRING129. The functional constraint suffix "\[FC]" is not part of the ObjectReference (7-2 §22.2 NOTE 1) and is not counted.

## Functions

### func Normalize

```go
func Normalize(s string) (string, error)
```

Normalize parses a reference in any supported form and returns its canonical string:

  - instance references "LD0/MMXU1.Hz.mag.f\[MX]"
  - MMS-style references "LD0/MMXU1$MX$Hz$mag$f"
  - class references "MMXU.Hz.mag.f\[MX]"

Input without "/" is read as a class reference. Normalization changes only the notation, never the content: an MMS reference becomes the bracketed FC form, and nothing is trimmed, case-folded or inferred.

### func SplitIndex

```go
func SplitIndex(component string) (name string, index int, ok bool, err error)
```

SplitIndex splits a path component into its name and an optional array element index, IEC 61850-7-2:2010 §6.1.2.3 ("The "(…)" shall indicate an array element") and §12.3.3.2.3 ("FCDA(NumArrayElement)", e.g. "phsAHar(3)"). It returns ok false for a component without an index. A malformed index — empty "()", a non-decimal "(x)", more than one "(1)(2)", text after ")" or a "(" without ")" — is an error.

## Types

### type ClassRef

```go
type ClassRef struct {
	// LNClass is the logical node class name, e.g. "MMXU".
	LNClass string
	// Path holds the data object and data attribute names.
	Path []string
	// FC is the functional constraint; empty when not specified.
	FC model.FunctionalConstraint
}
```

ClassRef is a class-level reference into the normative model: a logical node class followed by data object and data attribute names, with an optional functional constraint, e.g. "MMXU.Hz.mag.f\[MX]".

A class reference names what the standard defines; it says nothing about which logical device or instance a device exposes.

#### func ParseClass

```go
func ParseClass(s string) (ClassRef, error)
```

ParseClass parses a class-level reference of the form LNClass.DO.DA\[FC]. It fails with a [\*model.ReferenceError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ReferenceError) when the input contains a logical device separator: use [Parse](#func-parse) for instance references.

#### func (ClassRef) DataObject

```go
func (r ClassRef) DataObject() string
```

DataObject returns the first path element, the data object name, or "" when the reference points to the class.

#### func (ClassRef) String

```go
func (r ClassRef) String() string
```

String returns the canonical form, e.g. "MMXU.Hz.mag.f\[MX]".

#### func (ClassRef) Validate

```go
func (r ClassRef) Validate() error
```

Validate checks the structural invariants of the reference.

### type LNName

```go
type LNName struct {
	Prefix string
	Class  string
	Inst   string
}
```

LNName is a logical node instance name split into its parts, e.g. "Q0MMXU1" into prefix "Q0", class "MMXU" and instance "1".

#### func ParseLNName

```go
func ParseLNName(s string) (LNName, error)
```

ParseLNName splits a logical node instance name into prefix, class and instance number. The instance is the trailing run of digits and the class the four characters before it, which must be upper-case letters; anything before the class is the prefix. "LLN0" is the class LLN0 without prefix or instance.

The split is syntactic: whether the class exists is checked by resolving the reference against a profile.

#### func (LNName) String

```go
func (n LNName) String() string
```

String joins the parts back into the instance name.

### type Ref

```go
type Ref struct {
	// LD is the logical device name.
	LD string
	// LN is the logical node instance name, e.g. "LLN0" or "MMXU1".
	LN string
	// Path holds the data object and data attribute names. It is empty
	// when the reference points to a logical node.
	Path []string
	// FC is the functional constraint; empty when not specified.
	FC model.FunctionalConstraint
}
```

Ref is a parsed instance-level IEC 61850 object reference, as used on devices: LogicalDevice / LogicalNode . DataObject . DataAttribute, with an optional functional constraint in brackets.

Format: LD/LN.DO.DA\[FC], e.g. "LD0/MMXU1.Hz.mag.f\[MX]".

The format, the fields and the validation rules are those of the Ref type of github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850, so references convert between the two without loss.

#### func FromMMS

```go
func FromMMS(domain, item string) (Ref, error)
```

FromMMS builds a reference from an MMS domain and item ID of the form LN$FC$DO$DA. The domain and item ID are bounded by the MMS maxIdentifier size, as in [Ref.ToMMS](#func-ref-tomms).

#### func Parse

```go
func Parse(s string) (Ref, error)
```

Parse parses an instance-level object reference.

Accepted forms:

	LD/LN.DO.DA[FC]  full reference with functional constraint
	LD/LN.DO.DA      reference without functional constraint
	LD/LN            logical node reference
	LD               logical device reference

It fails with a [\*model.ReferenceError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ReferenceError) wrapping [model.ErrInvalidReference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrInvalidReference) on malformed input. Unknown functional constraints are accepted when they have two characters. Parse checks syntax only; use the resolver package to validate a reference against a namespace profile.

#### func ParseStrict

```go
func ParseStrict(s string) (Ref, error)
```

ParseStrict is like [Parse](#func-parse) and also enforces the length limits of IEC 61850-7-2:2010 Table 4 on the ObjectReference, the reference without its "\[FC]" suffix: at most MaxStrictLength characters, a logical device name of at most MaxLDLength and a path below it of at most MaxPathLength characters. The naming rules of 7-2 §22.2 (character set, start characters, name lengths) are checked separately by [Ref.ValidateNames](#func-ref-validatenames).

#### func (Ref) ToMMS

```go
func (r Ref) ToMMS() (domain, item string, err error)
```

ToMMS returns the MMS domain and item ID of the reference, following the IEC 61850-8-1 mapping LN$FC$DO$DA. A reference with a path needs a functional constraint.

The domain and the item ID are MMS identifiers: each is at most MaxMMSIdentifier characters (IEC 61850-8-1:2011 §8.1.3.2.2 and §7.3.1); longer names fail with a [\*model.ReferenceError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ReferenceError) that wraps both [model.ErrInvalidReference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrInvalidReference) and [model.ErrLimitExceeded](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ErrLimitExceeded). An array element "(n)" has no item ID form, because 8-1 addresses array elements with MMS alternate access, so a reference with an index fails too.

#### func (Ref) Validate

```go
func (r Ref) Validate() error
```

Validate checks the structural invariants of the reference:

  - LD is non-empty and at most MaxLDLength characters (IEC 61850-7-2:2010 §22.2 and Table 4)
  - Path and FC require LN
  - no empty path components
  - FC, when set, is two upper-case letters
  - no component contains a separator (/ . $ \[ ])
  - an array index "(n)" is a decimal number closing a path component (7-2:2010 §6.1.2.3)

#### func (Ref) ValidateNames

```go
func (r Ref) ValidateNames() error
```

ValidateNames checks the naming conventions of IEC 61850-7-2:2010 §22.2 that [Parse](#func-parse) leaves to the device, for references that must conform strictly (engineering tools, tests):

  - names use the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and "\_" only
  - the LD name starts with an alpha character
  - the LN-Prefix starts with an alpha character, and prefix plus instance number are at most MaxLNPrefixInstance characters
  - the LN class is four upper-case letters
  - the DataObjectName is at most MaxDataObjectName characters and starts with an upper-case letter
  - LN.DO.DA, without LD name and FC, is at most MaxFCDALength characters

The structural rules of [Ref.Validate](#func-ref-validate) are checked first. Errors are [\*model.ReferenceError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850-model/model#ReferenceError) values.

#### func (Ref) WithFC

```go
func (r Ref) WithFC(fc model.FunctionalConstraint) Ref
```

WithFC returns a copy of r with the functional constraint set to fc.
